findings.finding: GCP (84%-owned subsidiary, reported after AT last did) raised its FY2026 FFO I guide by EUR10m to EUR185-195m citing the LEG stake, so AT's consolidated absolute FY2026 FFO I guide (EUR275-305m) is likely to be lifted by roughly EUR8m (~3% of midpoint) in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 absolute-guide raise (per share unchanged) -> estimated -1.7%; Q3 2025 guide confirmed -> -6 to -8.7%; AT1 fell 1.5% on 11 Nov when GCP raised.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the raise is arithmetic from a public subsidiary release and AT's own 20 Oct 15%-accretion statement; AT1 did not rally on it (-1.5% on 11 Nov). What remains is whether AT also lifts the per-share range or gives a 2027 framing, which would show as a rally on the 11th if the market had assumed it.
findings.independence: AT ad-hoc/corporate news of 2026-10-20 (ca. 15% pro-rata FFO I accretion): https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/aroundtown-significantly-increases-its-share-in-german-residential-real-estate-through-gcps-financial-investment-in-leg-immobilien-se/5049b85d-6583-473e-8188-697fc85a53bf_en; Boersen-Zeitung on the GCP raise: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/grand-city-erhoeht-prognose-nach-einstieg-bei-leg

findings.finding: The LEG stake was funded at GCP with a EUR500m short-term bond and a EUR600m 2-year bridge, GCP LTV rose to 34% at Sep-30, and Berenberg questioned whether the stake is durable given refinancing needs; the Q3 release will show group LTV (43% at June) and the pro-forma, the line Goldman's Sell rests on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Goldman refinancing downgrade in October: intraday -2.4%; stock slid from EUR2.6 (May) to EUR1.35 (20 Oct) largely on rates/financing.
findings.original_quote: Berenberg-Analyst Kai Klose verwies nach der gestern gemeldeten Beteiligung auf möglichen Refinanzierungsbedarf und stellte die Dauerhaftigkeit des Investments infrage. (Berenberg's Kai Klose pointed to possible refinancing needs and questioned the durability of the investment.)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced after Goldman and Berenberg; what is new is the group LTV number itself. What the money buys is an asset at a >13% FFO yield, and AT is simultaneously repaying a EUR500m FRN early on 18 Dec, so the sign is only mildly negative.
findings.independence: GCP 9M release (funding details, LTV 34%): https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/grand-city-properties-s-a-announces-9m-2026-strong-operational-results-with-increased-guidance-for-fy-2026/fbb0f973-aa36-4163-936f-925056473540_en; Goldman Sell EUR1.30: https://www.boerse-global.de/aroundtown-aktie-goldman-sieht-refinanzierungsfalle/832533

findings.finding: JLL's Q3 2026 German office series shows vacancy up to 9.0% from 8.5% in Q2 (Frankfurt 12.1%, Duesseldorf 12%) and occupied stock down 377,000 sqm over 12 months, a headwind for AT's office vacancy and like-for-like in the Q3 KPIs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Office vacancy is a named driver of the Goldman Sell; no clean AT reaction history on vacancy prints alone.
findings.original_quote: Damit kletterte die Leerstandsquote auf 9,0 Prozent, nach 8,5 Prozent im zweiten Quartal und 7,9 Prozent vor einem Jahr. (The vacancy rate climbed to 9.0%, from 8.5% in Q2 and 7.9% a year ago.)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public series from October and AT's own like-for-like has held near +2.7-3.0% through it; a market-to-company transmission, so small. Priced if AT1 had not rallied 9% in 20 days.
